**Visual analysis:**

- **Plant**: Sugarcane (tall grass-like leaves, characteristic morphology)
- **Affected part**: Leaf blade
- **Key feature**: A prominent, broad **yellow/pale-yellow stripe running longitudinally along the midrib** of one leaf, while other leaves remain green. Some lower/older leaves are dry and brown (senescence or secondary damage). Purple-tinged stems visible in the background.

**Differential reasoning:**

| Class | Match |
|---|---|
| Yellow_Leaf | Broad midrib yellowing — classic Yellow Leaf Syndrome (SCYLV) symptom |
| Leaf_Scald | White/cream streaks along leaf margins, not central midrib |
| Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus | Mosaic/mottled green-yellow patches, not a continuous midrib stripe |
| Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv | Fine parallel streaks, not a broad central yellow band |
| Yellow_Spot | Discrete spots, not a longitudinal stripe |
| Brown_Spot | Brown oval spots, not present here |
| Pokkah_Boeng | Distorted/twisted young leaves, chlorotic patches near growing tip |
| Grassy_Shoot | Excessive narrow tillers, overall pale plant |
| Sett_Rot | Stem/sett rot, underground |

The dominant symptom — a **wide, continuous yellow band along the midrib** of an otherwise green leaf — is the hallmark of **Yellow Leaf** disease (Sugarcane Yellow Leaf Virus, SCYLV). The yellowing originates at the midrib and extends outward across the lamina, exactly as shown.

This midrib-centered longitudinal yellowing is the classic symptom of Yellow Leaf Syndrome (SCYLV). Other differentials (mosaic virus, streak mosaic, leaf scald) produce different patterns (mottling, fine streaks, marginal lesions) not seen here."}
